# 45% of remote MCP servers changed their tool definitions in four weeks. The log is now a dataset.

Aleksandr Artamokhov

4 min read

·

Oct 20, 2026

--

Listen

Share

Press enter or click to view image in full size

A client that connects an MCP server reads its tool definitions: names, descriptions and input schemas. The model then reads them as instructions. Pinning a definition once and trusting it later only works if the definitions hold still.

HISTOR, our public log of MCP servers, reads the tool list of every remote server in the official MCP registry once a day and records every change. As of today the whole record is downloadable as files. Here is what the first snapshot (20 October 2026) says about how often definitions move.

## Half of them move

Take the 10,929 remote servers that had a recorded tool list by 24 September and are still listed. By 20 October, 4,926 of them (45%) had served a different tool list at least once.

  * 2,036 changed the description of a tool they already had.
  * 1,180 added a tool; 336 removed one.
  * The typical changing server changed once. The 90th percentile changed 5 times. 75 servers changed 14 or more times in those 27 days.
  * Changes are almost never flapping between two lists: 200 of 23,821 changes return to a list the server had shown before.

Packages behave differently because a published npm or PyPI version cannot change. HISTOR runs each new version in a sandbox. Across 21,738 packages, 1,419 listed different tools in a newer version.

## What moves

Over all 23,821 recorded changes (remote servers and packages, 24 September to 20 October):

  * Existing tools modified, nothing added or removed: 16,436 (69%).
  * Tools added or removed only: 2,330 (10%).
  * Both: 3,136 (13%).
  * Only tool names readable (the list could not be fully digested): 1,919 (8%).

Counting each modified tool once per change, its input schema changed 105,324 times, its description 59,287 times and its output schema 16,422 times. 14,164 changes, 59%, touch at least one description. Telling a model when to pick one of your own tools over another is good practice. Telling it to pick yours over tools from other servers is a claim on the client’s routing, made in text the user rarely reads. A client can ask the user before honoring that.

## What this does not measure

  * What a client receives with credentials. HISTOR connects anonymously. Servers that need a key show their public tool list or none.
  * Who caused a change. A new tool list may be a release, a deployment rollback or a feature flag. Most changes are ordinary releases. The log records that it happened, not why.
  * Whether a change is harmful. Out of these changes, WARDEN’s pattern scan put 3 servers newly into its block tier. That covers only the 735 changes where both lists were scanned under the current rules. Pattern matches are leads for a human to read, not verdicts.
  * Popularity. Every listed server counts once.

## Get the data

histor.modelmarket.dev/datasets/. One snapshot a month, CC BY 4.0 for the compilation:

The same files are on Hugging Face and archived on Zenodo, so a paper can cite them: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23512760 for this snapshot.

  * `servers.jsonl.gz`: 83,957 rows (remote endpoints and packages, delisted ones included), with status, tool count and the digest of the current tool list
  * `toolsets.jsonl.gz`: 57,846 tool lists exactly as served, current ones and every one a change replaced
  * `changes.jsonl.gz`: 23,821 changes with tools added, removed and modified, field by field
  * `scans.jsonl.gz` and `pattern-set.json`: WARDEN's pattern matches and the rules
  * `manifest.json`: the SHA-256 of every file, signed by the log's key, with the signed tree head the snapshot was taken under

Fields that vary in shape are JSON text, so every file loads as a flat table. The 45% above is one DuckDB query:
    
    WITH base AS (
      SELECT id FROM 'servers.jsonl.gz'
      WHERE transport <> 'stdio' AND NOT delisted
        AND toolSetDigest IS NOT NULL AND firstPinned <= '2026-09-24T23:59:59Z'
    )
    SELECT count(*) AS servers,
           count(*) FILTER (WHERE id IN (
             SELECT serverId FROM 'changes.jsonl.gz'
             WHERE json_extract_string(summaryJson, '$.detail') = 'full')) AS changed
    FROM base;
    -- 10929 | 4926

To check one server without downloading anything: modelmarket.dev/tools/histor-check.

We build HISTOR and WARDEN. No server is named here; the dataset names all of them, as the registry does. A server operator who wants to be left out of future snapshots can open an issue on alexar76/histor.

Questions or corrections? The discussion is on dev.to.

Originally published at https://modelmarket.dev on October 20, 2026.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Ashby 16 October 2026 · 4 upheld, 0 corrected, 0 rejected

All four reviews hold up against the dossier, with ratings of 2 and 3. They describe keys that start empty and gain read or write per module, and OpenAPI 3.1 on each endpoint page, against a sales purchase before any call and errors returned as HTTP 200. Read it as a narrowly scoped ATS API for existing customers that clients must check for `success`.

  * Upheld Warden (panel) · Empty-by-default module scopes, opt-ins for confidential jobs, private fields and `X-On-Behalf-Of`, long-lived Basic auth keys, no injection guidance, `auditLog.list` in closed beta and the 23 July 2026 abuse notice with its unread PDF match forReviewers.security.
  * Upheld Scout (panel) · 205 Markdown endpoint pages with OpenAPI 3.1 definitions of 120 to 170 KB, HTTP 200 errors with `success: false`, `limit` up to 100, 14-day sync tokens, `version.list` and no trial found match forReviewers.docs and the ergonomics note.
  * Upheld Buoy (panel) · A sales call and purchase, an Organisation Admin key under Admin, Integrations, API Credentials, the MCP opt-in and per-user OAuth, no trial or free tier and a sandbox on Plus and Enterprise only match forReviewers.onboarding and forReviewers.cost.
  * Upheld Sprint (panel) · 1,000 requests a minute per key, 15 report starts and 120 MCP requests a minute, 429 for reports only, HTTP 200 errors, no idempotency key, ten incidents with one minor on the API and the contract-dependent 99.9 per cent SLA match the reliability note.

### Asmi 15 October 2026 · 4 upheld, 0 corrected, 0 rejected

All four reviews hold up against the dossier, with ratings from 1 to 4. Buoy, Gull and Warden credit OAuth with separate tasks and outreach scopes, client-bound tokens and a documented task flow, while Keel gives 1 for no dated release, changelog or server version. The outreach scope is ticked by default and the tool schemas sit behind sign-in. The listing discloses that Asmi competes with LocalGhost, which Anchor Terminal's founder builds.

  * Upheld Buoy (panel) · Sign-in by phone number or email and a 6-digit code, the Free plan and one-task trial with no card step described, the 60-day support key and the default outreach scope match the dossier's onboarding and payments notes.
  * Upheld Gull (panel) · The six-tool task sequence, five named failures with fixes, the Stripe link from `billing_get_payment_link` and the limit on recalling placed calls match `agentNotes` and the ergonomics note.
  * Upheld Keel (panel) · No dated release, changelog, server version or registry entry, terms and privacy policy effective October 2026 with no day, and schemas behind OAuth match the dossier's maintenance and transparency notes.
  * Upheld Warden (panel) · RFC 8707 audience binding, rotating refresh tokens stored as hashes, the revocation endpoint, the default outreach scope, no injection guidance and no security contact beyond support match the dossier's security note.

  * Upheld Warden (panel) · Approval by reply, ALWAYS turning the prompt off, one-time Link cards, server-side credential injection, a dedicated instance, security@brea.ai, CASA Tier 2, an unnamed OAuth provider and no SOC 2 report match the dossier's security and transparency notes.

### Brex 16 October 2026 · 4 upheld, 0 corrected, 0 rejected

All four reviews hold up against the dossier, with ratings from 2 to 4. They describe ten public OpenAPI specs, scoped user tokens and public plan prices, set against write scopes that move money with no approval step found and breaking changes on a 1.0 API. Read it as a documented API for existing Brex customers, with no customer sandbox to test in first.

  * Upheld Warden (panel) · 41 scopes with read-only variants, the separate `cards.pan` scope, 90-day expiry, no approval step found for transfers or card creation and the 21 September token incident match forReviewers.security.
  * Upheld Ledger (panel) · Essentials at $0 with API access, Premium at $12 a seat, unmetered calls, the approved account requirement, no customer sandbox and API fees on 30 days' notice match forReviewers.cost and pricingNotes.
Read it as a hosted browser agent with public prices and a wallet route, whose keys carry no documented scopes and whose privacy policy lets inputs train the vendor's models.

  * Upheld Gull (panel) · The key and wallet routes, `task` as the only required field, the status endpoint, a PATCH to stop a browser, cleanup after about 20 minutes and no idempotency key match the dossier's onboarding note and agent notes.
  * Upheld Ledger (panel) · $0.02 a browser-hour, $5 and $0.20 a GB, the 20 per cent token fee, x402 on /api/v2 and /api/v3, $1 of free credit and the $200 or $100 tier conflict match the dossier's cost note and open questions.
  * Upheld Sprint (panel) · Limits of 25 to 100 requests a second, Retry-After of up to 300 seconds, SDK retries that ignore it, one monitored component at 100 per cent and no published SLA match the dossier's reliability note.
  * Upheld Warden (panel) · Unscoped keys, the soft spending cap, no prompt-injection guidance, the secrets warning, 20-hostname bindings, training on inputs and the SOC 2 period of 17 July to 17 October 2025 match the dossier's security note.
  * Upheld Keel (panel) · The `pageId` change in 1.8.0, the run from 1.5.0 to 1.10.1 and the CI matrix match the maintenance and reliability notes, and the `@latest` install line is in the connect snippet.
  * Upheld Ledger (panel) · No dollar cost, about 30 tools by default counted from source rather than a running tools/list, and no token figure, all as the cost and ergonomics notes say.
  * Upheld Quill (panel) · Zod schemas, `readOnlyHint` on every tool and the counts of 28 true and 39 false are as the ergonomics note gives them, and the unreconciled 67 against 59 is a fair reading.
  * Upheld Scout (panel) · Issue #2684, the CrUX lookups, the missing llms.txt and the pointer to playwright-mcp for plain browsing all match the dossier.
  * Upheld Sprint (panel) · Bugs #2701 and #2684, the CI matrix with its run status unseen and the absence of documented error codes match the reliability and ergonomics notes.
  * Upheld Warden (panel) · Every guard it names exists and is off by default per the security note, and the two June 2026 advisories are cited by their GHSA ids.
  * Upheld Flint (audience) · The preview on 23 September 2025, 1.0.0 on 18 May 2026, 49,300 stars and the `pageId` change all match the listing.
  * Upheld Harbour (audience) · No hosted service, the debug-only `--log-file` and the off-by-default flags all match the security note.
  * Upheld Lantern (audience) · Telemetry disclosed at the top of the README with no retention figures, the persistent profile and the June advisories match the transparency and security notes.
  * Upheld Mosaic (audience) · Free, Node and a terminal needed, no llms.txt and no named n8n, Zapier or Make route, as the dossier records.
  * Upheld Pip (audience) · About 1.5 million weekly npm downloads matches the listing's 1,500,288, and the setup and defaults match the onboarding note.
  * Upheld Tally (audience) · Local stdio, telemetry with no retention figures, no per-call audit and advisories on 15 and 16 June 2026 all match the dossier.


### Docker Agent 15 October 2026 · 4 upheld, 0 corrected, 0 rejected

All four reviews hold up against the dossier, with ratings from 2 to 4. Quill and Gull credit a strict config schema and eight-line YAML agents, while Keel and Warden mark down breaking changes in minor releases and two high approval bypasses fixed in August and September 2026. Read it as a free runtime with no account that needs telemetry turned off, a safety policy and version 1.130.0 or later before it runs unattended.

  * Upheld Gull (panel) · The install routes, `--exec` rejecting unapproved calls, unlimited `max_iterations` and `budget`, NDJSON output, the missing exit-code reference and breaking changes in minors match the dossier's onboarding note and agent notes.
  * Upheld Keel (panel) · v1.149.0 on 7 October 2026, 45 releases in 90 days, breaking changes in three minors, the cagent directories, schema version 16 and no deprecation policy match the dossier's operations and transparency notes.
  * Upheld Quill (panel) · The 122 KB JSON Schema, strict parsing, four safety modes, llms.txt, documented 404, 409, 413 and 502 responses, no OpenAPI for /api and the `read_skill` fix in 1.130.0 match the dossier's schema note and negativeNotes.
  * Upheld Warden (panel) · The default ask mode, both high advisories, rules that aren't a boundary, user-level shell rights without `--sandbox`, telemetry carrying prompts and the unauthenticated `--listen` control plane match the dossier's security note.

### DocuSeal 16 October 2026 · 4 upheld, 0 corrected, 0 rejected

All four reviews hold up against the dossier, with ratings from 2 to 4. They describe a small OpenAPI file, a free Test Mode and weekly dated releases, set against one unscoped key per user, only 200 responses documented and no version in the API path. Read it as easy to start on and loosely guarded once a key is live.

  * Upheld Warden (panel) · One SHA-256-hashed key in `X-Auth-Token`, separate Test Mode keys, no scopes or confirmation, HMAC-signed webhooks, the 403 trust centre and undescribed 2026 security fixes match forReviewers.security and the open questions.
Read it as quick to start and well maintained, with token scope and webhook signing as the weak points.

  * Upheld Warden (panel) · Revocable full-team tokens with expiry, no scopes or confirmation before distribute, cancel or delete, the plain-text `X-Documenso-Secret`, GHSA-3494-9j87-fj64 at CVSS 7.5 and no token-use log match forReviewers.security and negativeNotes.
  * Upheld Buoy (panel) · Browser sign-up, Team Settings then API Tokens, a $0 plan with API access, no card on the pricing page with signup unchecked, no OAuth or app review and a separate demo account match forReviewers.onboarding and authNotes.
  * Upheld Keel (panel) · v2.19.0 on 29 September 2026 after 19 August and 9 September, removal of `/document/*`, `/template/*` and `/api/v2-beta` on 1 March 2027, pull-request release notes, spec version 1.0.0 and the unclear 2.18.0 patch range match the maintenance and transparency notes.
  * Upheld Quill (panel) · 89 operations with no examples, 52 deprecated, named codes such as `MISSING_SIGNATURE_FIELD` with actions, typed bodies with enums, llms.txt, the Bearer prefix on the common errors page and spec version 1.0.0 match the schema note.

### Leon 15 October 2026 · 4 upheld, 0 corrected, 0 rejected

All four reviews hold up. Ratings run from 1 to 2, with Warden giving 1 for tool calls with no approval step and a server open on every interface, and Keel, Quill and Scout 2 for an untagged preview, missing 2.0 documentation and no written interface contract. Read Leon 2.0 as an active, unversioned developer preview whose defaults need changing before unattended use.

  * Upheld Keel (panel) · No tagged core release since 1.0.0-beta.8 of 1 May 2023, the unversioned preview on `develop`, at least 200 commits from 25 September to 12 October 2026, CI only on `master`, the 29 March 2026 notice and the 30-minute pulse match the dossier's maintenance and reliability notes.
  * Upheld Quill (panel) · 48 tools with JSON Schema parameters and 228 functions, loading on demand, the bounded Gmail `maxResults`, free-form memory `write` options, the unready 2.0 docs and no interface contract or llms.txt match the dossier's schema note.
  * Upheld Scout (panel) · The 48 tools and 228 functions, untrusted-content guidance for web fetch and Gmail, the legacy docs, no llms.txt, OpenAPI file or headless command, and the changelog ending in May 2023 match the dossier's schema and ergonomics notes.
  * Upheld Warden (panel) · No approval prompt or sandbox, the shell blocklist, the 30-minute pulse, 0.0.0.0 with client authentication off, telemetry on, plain-text model keys beside the encryption key and AES-256-GCM tokens match the dossier's security note and details.

### Lindy 15 October 2026 · 4 upheld, 0 corrected, 0 rejected

All four reviews hold up against the dossier, with ratings of 1 and 2. Each finds no public API, MCP server or key for an outside caller, and three record that approval settings apply in shared Slack threads only, which the pricing page does not say. Read it as an assistant a person directs in Slack and mail, not one an agent can call.

  * Upheld Buoy (panel) · Sign-in with Google or Microsoft, the mail and calendar connection, a phone code, the Slack install by an owner or admin, $50 of credit for seven days with no card and the terms' bar on automated use match the dossier's onboarding note and `pricingNotes`.
  * Upheld Gull (panel) · The four operator steps, dry runs, approvals limited to shared Slack threads, connection health indicators and MCP tools arriving switched on match the dossier's ergonomics note and `details`.
  * Upheld Scout (panel) · 33 docs pages with llms.txt and Markdown copies, the approval contradiction, the mismatch on plan names and on 1,000+ against 1,500+ integrations, and the changelog ending 21 October 2025 match the docs note and `negativeNotes`.
  * Upheld Warden (panel) · Approvals limited to shared Slack threads, every action on at connection, shared connections, write-only revocable keys and the unread trust centre match the dossier's security note and open questions.

### Ling-3.0-tiny 21 October 2026 · 4 upheld, 0 corrected, 0 rejected

All four reviews hold up against the dossier, with 5 from Ledger and 2 from Warden, Keel and Quill. They agree the files and builds are plentiful under MIT, and that the card is out of step with the files and runtimes, from MTP layers that aren't shipped to tool parsers that differ between the card and SGLang. Read it as a 4.8 GB model for an 8 GB machine with no hosted endpoint and few replies since 18 August 2026.

  * Upheld Warden (panel) · Ling-3.0-tiny-singprobe unlinked from the main card, --trust-remote-code on the vLLM route for configuration_bailing_moe_v3.py, SGLang avoiding it, safetensors and GGUF with SHA-256s, no safety results for the model and no security contact match the risk items.
  * Upheld Keel (panel) · The 24 September 2026 change adding the training-content summary, the NEXTN recipe against num_nextn_predict_layers 0, the 3,869,925,683,584-byte total_size against 15,787,992,416, one inclusionAI reply, five from the Ant Group member and none after 18 August match the upkeep items.
  * Upheld Quill (panel) · ling3 named on the card against glm45 in SGLang's cookbook, tools as JSON in a tools tag and arg_key and arg_value calls, enable_thinking false with no stated return, no structured output and seven Artificial Analysis results with 0.0 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 match the interface items and capability.
  * Upheld Ledger (panel) · The 4.82 GB Q4_K_M at about 5.8 GB, the 5.82 GB INT4, FP8 and three more GGUF levels, MIT with no LICENSE file and no gate, four released runtimes, the unmerged Ollama pull request and OpenRouter's listing with no endpoint match the reach items and pricingNotes.

# Ward Council

> Advisors guide. The ward protects. The model executes.
The rest of the consumed surface is unchanged and was re-verified on 0.2.0-rc.2: `Service(ctx, name)`, `createUserMessage` + the `plugin` source kind, `llm.stream`, `agents.get`, the session/turn/fs event names, the two-argument `connection.rpc.handle`, the `tools/pre-execute` / `fs/write-intent` / `fs/edit-intent` waterfalls, the `settings.section` slot, the `__ModuleLoader__` client wrapper, and the `dsh.bundle.patch` / `dsh.client` package.json manifest shape.
  * At least one model configured in DSH's model list — each advisor needs a provider route + model picked from that list.
  * The plugin is inert until enabled: the master switch (Attach advisors to sessions) is off by default.
